overview.description: Giltspiel is a four-player fixed-partnership trump trick game from Tyrol that combines five-trick play with open betting on three figures: Gleich (sets), Hanger (sequences), and Spiel (majority of tricks).

history.origins: Giltspiel was documented in Tyrol as an old game by the mid-19th century and is treated as the ancestor of Perlaggen.
timeline: 1853: Mentioned in an Innsbruck Perlaggen book as an established older game.
2015: Hubert Auer documented active modern play in Fiss, Serfaus, and Ladis.
2024: Rules documentation updated with detailed betting, showdown, and endgame procedures.
history.evolution: Historical variants introduced wild cards and developed into Perlaggen; base Giltspiel has no wild cards.
history.cultural: Table talk and visible signaling are part of normal play, and bluffing is explicitly accepted.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, partners opposite.
setup.deck: 32-card German suits (bells, acorns, hearts, leaves), rank high to low: A K O U 10 9 8 7.
setup.dealing: Deal five cards each clockwise in two packets (2+3 or 3+2). Turn the next card up to set trump suit.

rules.objective: Be the first partnership to reach the agreed target (usually 11 or 15 points).
rules.gameplay: Eldest hand leads. On each trick, a player who has led suit may either follow suit or play trump; if unable to follow suit they may play any card. If any trump is played, highest trump wins; otherwise highest card of led suit wins. Winner leads next. Cards remain face up in front of each player in play order. Three figures are scored each deal: Gleich (best set of equal ranks), Hanger (best suited sequence), and Spiel (team that wins at least 3 of 5 tricks). Betting on each figure can happen during play and can be conceded, seen, or raised. Play stops immediately when Spiel is decided or conceded, and unresolved Gleich/Hanger are settled by staged showdown reveals.
keyRules: Initial value of each figure is 1 point and can be increased by accepted bets.
Bets on a figure alternate by team; a team that just had its bet seen cannot bet that figure again until the other team bets it.
Any player who bet or saw Gleich or Hanger must later prove they hold at least a minimal valid instance of that figure or incur penalty.
When Spiel is decided early, trick play stops immediately and showdown begins for unresolved figures.

strategy.basic: Use early betting to pressure opponents into conceding figures they likely cannot improve.
strategy.intermediate: Track revealed cards and showdown obligations so you know when a bluff is impossible to sustain.
strategy.advanced: Conceding Spiel at the right time can force opponents to show first in showdown, revealing information before your team commits.
tips: Preserve flexible trumps because you can trump even when you could have followed suit.
Do not over-signal to partner; visible communication is legal, but extra information helps opponents too.

difficulty.easy: Makes legal plays and only bets with obvious strong figures.
difficulty.medium: Balances trick control with selective betting and occasional concessions.
difficulty.hard: Models reveal obligations, alternation rights on each figure, and uses controlled bluff lines in betting and showdown.

considerations: Agent must track separate value ladders and betting turn rights for Gleich, Hanger, and Spiel.
Showdown requires stateful reveal logic and penalties when a bettor/caller cannot validate a figure.

phases.label: Deal and Turn Trump
phases.notes: Deal 5 cards to each player and expose next card to determine trump suit.

phases.label: Trick Play and Figure Betting
phases.notes: Play up to five tricks while betting can interrupt at any point.

phases.label: Showdown for Gleich and Hanger
phases.notes: Teams alternate showing, contesting, conceding, or betting unresolved figures.

phases.label: Score Figures
phases.notes: Award Gleich, Hanger, and Spiel values (including bet adjustments and penalties) and update partnership totals.

ante.reason: Giltspiel has no ante or pot contribution.

deal.description: Deal five cards each and expose the trump indicator card.

buy_market.reason: No market purchase mechanic in Giltspiel.

buy_stock.reason: No stock buying mechanic in Giltspiel.

fold.description: Concede a specific figure to opponents (called good).
fold.constraints: Applies to current unresolved figure bet.

check.reason: Giltspiel betting responses are concede, see, or raise; no check action token.

call.description: See (hold) a bet to accept higher figure value.
call.constraints: Opposing team response to a bet.

bet.description: Propose increasing value of Gleich, Hanger, or Spiel by one point.
bet.constraints: Allowed at legal timing for the acting team and figure.

raise.description: Counter-bet to increase figure value by one more point.
raise.constraints: Only as response chain to active figure bet.

declare.reason: Declarations are modeled via reveal and betting actions.

reveal_hand.description: Reveal cards during showdown to contest or validate Gleich/Hanger claims.
reveal_hand.constraints: Showdown phase and validation checks only.

award_pot.description: Apply figure outcomes, penalties, and update partnership score.

play_card.description: Play one card to trick with Giltspiel follow-or-trump obligations.
play_card.constraints: If able to follow led suit, player may follow suit or play trump; otherwise any card.

draw.reason: No draw mechanic after the initial deal.

discard.reason: Played cards remain visible as ordered trick history, not a discard action.

pass.reason: No pass action in base Giltspiel flow.

bid.reason: Figure betting is represented by bet/call/raise rather than a separate bid action token.

meld.reason: No meld declarations separate from Gleich/Hanger reveal process.

go_out.reason: Rounds end by figure resolution, not empty-hand shedding.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: No draw phase after the initial five-card deal.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Trick cards remain as open history rows instead of discard pile operations.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Base Giltspiel uses no wildcards or action cards.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Giltspiel is a partnership trick and figure betting game, not a shedding game.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: No tableau capture mechanic exists in Giltspiel.

edgeCases.text: A player with led suit may still choose to play trump instead of following suit.
When Spiel is conceded or mathematically won (third trick complete), trick play stops immediately and unresolved figures go to showdown.
Any player who bet or saw Gleich/Hanger must prove a minimal valid example or team loses right to that figure and suffers penalty.

customLogicNeeded: Separate betting ladders and turn rights for each figure (Gleich, Hanger, Spiel).
Immediate transition to showdown when Spiel is decided or conceded.
Showdown alternation with concede/contest/bet options and validation penalties.

customActions.description: Concede Spiel figure immediately (das Spiel ist gut).
Reveal additional cards to keep Gleich or Hanger contested during showdown.

engine.deckDescription: The deck is a thirty-two-card German-suited pack (William Tell or similar pattern): four suits with eight ranks each (Ace, King, Ober, Unter, 10, 9, 8, 7) for trick play with declarer versus defenders.
engine.suitDescription: The four German suits are Bells (Schellen), Acorns (Eichel), Hearts (Herz), and Leaves (Grün); the game is traditionally played with Swiss or German regional patterns such as William Tell.
engine.rankDescription: The rank set is Stripped_32: eight ranks per suit in German order from high to low Ace, King, Ober, Unter, 10, 9, 8, 7, used for trick-taking with contract-specific trump and matador rules.
engine.dealPattern: 5 cards each in two packets; next card turned for trump.

hero.title: GILTSPIEL
hero.subtitle: Tyrolean Figure-Betting Trump Game
hero.tagline: Win tricks, win figures, and win the betting war.

synthesis.shortDescription: Partnership trump trick game where Gleich, Hanger, and Spiel are scored and aggressively bet during play and showdown.

prompts.human: Giltspiel: coordinate with partner, pressure figures through betting, and switch cleanly into showdown when Spiel is settled.
prompts.ai: Game: Giltspiel. Four players in fixed teams. Deal 5 from a 32-card German deck, turn trump, play up to 5 tricks while betting on Gleich, Hanger, and Spiel, then resolve showdown and score to 11 or 15.

scoring.description: Each deal awards figure values for Gleich, Hanger, and Spiel, with values increased by accepted bets and modified by concessions or penalties.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach agreed target score (typically 11 or 15) wins.

penalties.failed_validation: If a player who bet or saw Gleich/Hanger cannot show a valid example, team is penalized and cannot win that figure.

scoring.splitRules: Partnership totals are cumulative across deals.

nullReasons.targetScore: Target score is agreed before the session, commonly 11 or 15.
nullReasons.cardValues: Points are awarded for figure outcomes (Gleich, Hanger, Spiel) and bets, not for individual card point values.
